newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venzuela public sector strike in its seventh day.
newsitem.headline: Venzuela public sector strike in its seventh day.

text.p: Hundreds of striking Venezuelan public sector workers marched on Congress on Tuesday demanding bonuses they said they had been promised.
The strike, billed as a 48-hour stoppage when it began last Tuesday, is the most serious labour conflict since President Rafael Caldera took office in February 1994.

"The only person responsible is the government, which owes us money," said Carlos Borges, president of the National Federation of Public Workers. Union leaders have said the government owes staff, who earn an average monthly wage of $106, a total of $212 million in bonuses promised in February.

Banging pots and waving banners reading "One doesn't have to go to Rwanda to see hunger," the strikers were joined by a group of blind salesmen protesting a recent municipal ordinance that forbids street selling in the city centre.
The Labour Ministry has played down the strike, saying less than 10 percent of the unions' 1.3 million members have stopped work -- a claim rejected by union heads.
Borges said union leaders would meet with President Rafael Caldera and congressional leaders on Thursday to seek a solution.
